title: The Dog in the Manger

full_text:
A grumpy, ill-tempered farm dog, seeking a comfortable place to sleep during the heat of the afternoon, climbed into the manger of the barn. He curled himself up upon a soft, fragrant bed of sweet clover and golden oat hay, falling into a comfortable doze.

Presently, the tired oxen returned from the fields, weary and hungry after a long day of plowing the heavy furrow. They stepped into the stall and reached their broad muzzles toward the manger to eat the fresh hay that their master had provided.

Instantly, the dog woke up in a savage fury. He sprang to his feet, bared his teeth, and barked viciously at the oxen, snapping at their noses whenever they tried to take a mouthful of the hay!

"Stand back, you clumsy brutes!" snarled the dog, bristling with spite.

One patient ox looked down at the snarling hound and sighed with sorrowful indignation:

"What a miserable, selfish creature you are! You cannot eat the hay yourself, for grass is no food for a dog; yet you refuse to let those who can eat it satisfy their honest hunger. You enjoy nothing, except preventing others from enjoying what is theirs!"
moral: Do not begrudge to others what you cannot enjoy yourself.
